heading: Depth and width change loss little across moderate shapes at fixed parameter count
definition: at a fixed parameter count, depth, width and other architecture details change loss only slightly within a wide range.
summary: Several independent groups reproduce modest architecture effects within bounded shape ranges in text models below 1B and at 1–10B parameters. Extreme shapes and full PostLN can break this pattern; evidence at 10–100B covers narrower architecture comparisons, including MoE granularity, while models above 100B remain unassessed.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 at <1B and 1–10B for bounded central text-model shape ranges. R0 for quantified 10–100B MoE granularity, alongside narrower qualitative architecture checks; broad dense shape robustness remains unassessed there. ? above 100B. Records with unstated size cannot establish a scale-specific level.
suggested_status.reason: Independent architecture comparisons reproduce modest central-range effects: reviewed LiteTransformerSearch tests fixed decoder budgets, and reviewed Panda compares fixed-parameter/token models at 1B and 3B. Fine-Grained MoE supplies larger-scale granularity comparisons. This status applies to the bounded regularity; full-PostLN divergence challenges unrestricted architecture-detail robustness. counts: versions.V4.studies_by_size supplies <1B, 1-10B and 10-100B coverage but no >100B entry; versions.V4.verdicts includes both support and challenges. Same-author extensions must not be mistaken for independent reproduction; versions.V4.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original records overlap.
suggested_status.open_questions: Broad equal-token dense shape sweeps at 10–100B and above 100B; convergence and per-shape tuning controls; instruction/chat and reasoning-training comparisons; explicit metric-specific thresholds for slight effects; whether normalization and information-access failures persist under architecture-appropriate training recipes.

source.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
source.authors: Jared Kaplan; Sam McCandlish; Tom Henighan; Tom B. Brown; Benjamin Chess; Rewon Child; Scott Gray; Alec Radford; Jeffrey Wu; Dario Amodei

original_result.setup: The original study varied depth, width, attention-head dimension and feed-forward ratio while holding non-embedding parameter count fixed.
original_result.result: Test loss varied by only a few percent; a 6-layer, width-4288 model reached loss within 3% of a 48-layer, width-1600 model. Models with fewer than 2 layers or extreme depth-to-width ratios deviated significantly.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.basis: counts: versions.V4.studies_by_size has no >100B entry. Neither pack supplies a comparison above that scale.

untested.what: Broad dense language-model depth/width sweeps at 10–100B with quantified held-out loss, matched parameters and matched training budgets.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V4.studies_by_size includes 10-100B, so the gap concerns test design rather than absence of that bucket. PaLM tests one qualitative layer toggle; the 14B MoE study tests one placement change; Fine-Grained MoE varies granularity rather than dense depth/width. Their untested-parts lines preserve this gap.

untested.what: Whether a broad shape-insensitive range persists through instruction/chat fine-tuning or reasoning training.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V4.studies_by_stage has no instruct/chat or reasoning entries, while preference/RL is present. Neither pack supplies such a shape sweep. Hourglass tests long-context fine-tuning, so fine-tuning in general is not untested.

untested.what: Factorial separation of the larger Hourglass comparisons' architecture dimensions and equal-token validation of HyperCLOVA's shallow-wide result.
untested.basis: The studies' untested-parts/problems lines identify these missing controls. Hourglass jointly changes depth, width and FFN shape; HyperCLOVA's arXiv:2506.22403#R1 uses equal wall-clock training with 15% more tokens for the shallow-wide model. counts: versions.V4.studies_by_size establishes coverage of the relevant size range but does not establish these controls.

wording_issues.issue: Parameter and resource matching differ: decoder/non-embedding, total, active and trainable parameters are distinct; equal FLOPs or wall-clock time also changes the comparison. HyperCLOVA's equal-time comparison changes token exposure. Synthetic ICL holds nominal N=L·d fixed without establishing matched actual Transformer parameter counts, so it cannot determine V4. CART has inconsistent stored-parameter counts.
Near-invariance has bounded, size-dependent ranges. Shallow or deep/narrow endpoints and vocabulary/rank bottlenecks change both loss-effect magnitude and the direction of depth preference.

The unrestricted phrase includes changes producing divergence or substantial degradation: normalization placement, TextNCA schedules/conditioning, ELM synaptic integration and coarse versus fine-grained MobileMoE experts. MobileMoE's substantially lower-loss comparison uses coarse g=1 as baseline for g≥2 at fixed active and total parameters. The separate g=16 versus g=8 comparison reports loss reduction below 0.01 with approximately 50% more wall-clock time; Figure 5 runs use the same data for 500B tokens. Local head-count or wiring robustness does not establish robustness to all these interventions.

No common effect threshold is specified. Perplexity deviation from a median, additional reducible loss and percentage change in total loss have different denominators. Transformer-XL's maximum validation-perplexity deviation is less than 7% from the median at the given decoder parameter count across aspect ratios [8, 323]. Video AR-k=4 validation flow MSE has a spread approximately 8.06% above its within-factorization minimum after 1M training videos; its wide-shallow model has 96.91M parameters. This supports a bounded range, while a 4.5% protein-loss improvement limits scope.

Some supporting comparisons test a single matched pair or selected shapes, without locating a broad interval. TTT-E2E, the 160M depth/FFN control and CART supply local comparisons; MDM-Prime supplies selected depth/width configurations.

Evidence mixes final training loss, fitted limit training loss, training NLL, held-out loss, task-specific perplexity and flow MSE. PaLM reports an unspecified quality metric, while optical and vision findings concern accuracy. These outcomes cannot establish one numerical loss-invariance threshold.

Small absolute loss differences can encode consistent architecture preferences and substantial resource consequences. Variable-width profiles have reported fitted compute savings; Fine-Grained MoE has training-step savings; residual design and layer-wise allocation yield systematic preferences.

Training horizon and evaluation stage are unspecified. Parameter-matched byte models have large shape effects at 16M bytes (245 steps), challenging V4 in that condition; longer-budget results show small effects among the shallowest shapes tested, with FP32 rankings changing with budget. Cosine MoE differences shrink with convergence: WikiText-103 uses 50K steps/1.64B tokens, while OpenWebText separately reports approximately 6.5 epochs over 507M corpus tokens, with inconsistent duration reporting. Hourglass's larger perplexity gap after long-context extension is measured on a different corpus and at different context lengths; no matched Proof-pile before/after comparison isolates a fine-tuning effect.

method_sensitivity.what: Full PostLN diverges in the optimizer study. Under Cramming's aggressive one-cycle recipe, Post-LN MLM loss is 7.54 versus the Modified Transformer baseline's 1.89. MatGPT reports similar NeoX/LLaMA losses at matched shape under Adam with a 1M-token batch, but lower LLaMA training and validation losses under LAMB with a 4M-token batch at 1.7B and 6.7B. The LAMB advantage is unquantified, so it cannot establish a V4 limitation. The smooth-training-loss shape experiment tunes learning rate and batch size separately for each architecture.

CompleteP broadens the near-optimal depth/width range relative to µP. DepthBench's depth preferences depend on residual design; at 400M, increasing L from 16 to 32 changes HC loss from 2.751 to 2.718 and Full AttnRes loss from 2.729 to 2.699, small changes compatible with V4. Other-scale qualitative preferences do not establish large loss effects. The separate AttnRes architecture sweep shifts the preferred dmodel/Lb from approximately 60 to 45, with optimum losses 1.847 and 1.802 respectively. That sweep does not specify Full versus Block AttnRes, and the optimum shift alone does not determine fixed-parameter shape sensitivity.

Vocabulary/embedding-rank bottlenecks change depth preferences. Distance-adaptive attention's advantage depends on bottleneck dimension and retaining full-dimensional local representations. Small Qwen query read-point shifts have much smaller effects than network-input queries everywhere; Extender responds more to removing its FFN state input than to local query changes.

Cosine MoE topology gaps shrink with training. WikiText-103 uses 50K steps and 1.64B tokens; OpenWebText is separately described as approximately 6.5 epochs over 507M corpus tokens, inconsistent with applying the general marathon duration uniformly. The byte-model sweep challenges V4 at 16M bytes (245 steps): parameter-matched shapes span 2.835–3.477 FP32 loss and 3.426–4.162 ternary loss. At 130M bytes, only the three shallowest shapes were tested and their loss differences are small; this is not a full longer-budget replication of the shape grid. Fine-Grained MoE granularity gains grow with duration. Dense-FFN granularity variants start behind the baseline and reach much smaller final gaps.

method_sensitivity.factor: Evaluation corpus, context and training stage
method_sensitivity.what: LLaMA's fixed-size sweep is flatter on LAMBADA than WIKITEXT-2. YOCO's depth effect differs between those corpora and recursive layouts. At 8B, conventional/Hourglass pretraining validation PPL is 13.37/13.31 averaged over four datasets. After identical YaRN extension, Proof-pile PPL is 7.39/7.10 at 4k and 4.79/4.55 at 64k. Corpus and context also change, so these comparisons do not isolate fine-tuning as the cause of the larger gap. Target-tuned learned splines qualitatively improve FineWeb and CodeSearchNet-Java/Python validation loss, but exact losses are figure-only and V4 is cannot_determine. Reported transfer outliers concern transfer to other datasets.

HyperCLOVA's equal-time shallow-wide model sees 15% more tokens. Terraformer approaches the dense baseline with more data after a matched-data loss gap: its later loss is 1.59 versus dense 1.57, a near-match compatible with V4 at that checkpoint, but using 1.4 times the baseline's data. Gemstones' loss/FLOPs frontier varies parameter count and training tokens. Translation depth/width comparisons control similar additional training FLOPs; matching non-embedding counts for selected variants does not establish fixed total parameters because embedding counts differ. These Gemstones and translation comparisons cannot determine V4's fixed-parameter loss sensitivity and are retained as comparison-design coverage.

LiteTransformerSearch fixes decoder parameters and warns that embeddings can mask its ranking relationship. On WikiText-103, Transformer-XL perplexity deviates by less than 7% from the median at the given decoder parameter count across aspect ratios [8, 323]. Variable-Width Transformers' MoE comparison matches total parameters while changing active parameters; its small loss changes support V4. Structured FastFood/block-diagonal comparisons use trainable parameters. Byte-model shape matching fixes total parameters while embedding share varies; its short-budget shape differences challenge V4, whereas the tested longer-budget subset supports small differences.

Weakening load balance shifts preferred expert granularity from around 12 to 6–8 at fixed total and active parameters. Routed-model loss surfaces are nearly coincident for routing frequencies R={0.25,0.5,1.0}; the slight R=0.25 deviation remains compatible with V4. Stronger departures with a single routed layer are a separate condition. Shared-expert-ratio effects in the fixed-total/active-parameter study remain small, while activated-expert sweeps have U-shaped loss relationships whose magnitudes are unavailable. The separate shared-expert ablation in arXiv:2507.17702 does not establish fixed total parameters and has conflicting activation-ratio descriptions; it cannot determine V4.

Cycle versus Sequence sharing changes recursive-Transformer NLL, and extensive LoopMDM looping worsens loss. Meta Expert's tested topology effects remain small but its preferred topology depends on depth. Reversing selected heterogeneous width allocations raises loss while preserving projection shapes and the stated architecture score.

method_sensitivity.factor: Scale and fitted versus directly measured effects
method_sensitivity.what: Holistic Scaling's near-optimal hidden-dimension band widens with compute scale. Its fitted width-ratio sweep uses (K+1)·dm/d: at 10^18 FLOPs, predicted loss spreads are 1.096% for E=0 and 0.554% with a nonzero floor; at 3×10^20 FLOPs they are 0.367% and 0.286%, respectively. These are fitted predictions, not a uniform below-0.5% bound. HEP taggers' preferred aspect ratio changes across 10M–100M under per-shape tuning, while shallow within-size loss dependence supports V4. ELM networks' preferred recurrent fraction rises with network size, but this unquantified optimum shift cannot determine V4. The Chinchilla reanalysis predicts shape sensitivity from a fitted surface instead of independently training a controlled shape sweep.
